description: STORM multi-perspective research ledger. Each technique is recorded with source, date, problem, evidence strength, applicability, cost, accessibility, privacy, and selected/rejected decision.

A_advertising_transparency.summary: Studied Meta Ad Library, Google Ads Transparency Center, and EU DSA Transparency Database. Key principles: task-oriented entry points, advertiser provenance, deep links to individual ads, downloadable data, field explanations, empty states, progressive disclosure.

techniques.name: Meta Ad Library API pattern
techniques.problem: Provide public transparency into political/social-issue advertising
techniques.evidence_strength: HIGH — production system with documented API
techniques.applicability: HIGH — task-oriented search by keyword/advertiser, deep links to individual ads, downloadable data
techniques.accessibility_impact: POSITIVE — clear entry points, field explanations
techniques.rationale: Meta Ad Library's task-oriented search (by keyword, advertiser, category) and individual-ad deep links directly inform the 'Explore Evidence' section design. The ManiPsych dashboard already has per-ad deep links (#adintel-ad=<rid>) but lacks a unified task-oriented search entry point.

techniques.name: Google Ads Transparency Center — per-ad detail page
techniques.problem: Show advertiser provenance, campaign details, ad creatives per ad
techniques.applicability: HIGH — per-ad detail page with provenance, creative, dates, format
techniques.rationale: The per-ad detail page pattern (provenance + creative + dates + format) directly informs the 'AdEvidenceRecord' canonical schema. Each ad should have a detail page showing collection metadata, platform, dates, and content.

techniques.name: EU DSA — mandatory transparency fields
techniques.problem: Mandate transparency in digital advertising — targeting parameters, advertiser identity, reach
techniques.applicability: MEDIUM — ManiPsych is defensive research, not a regulated platform, but the field-explanation principle applies
techniques.rationale: DSA's principle of field-level explanations (every visible field has a documented meaning) directly informs the indicator dictionary requirement. Every indicator must have a plain-language definition, formula, and limitation.

B_hierarchical_persuasion.summary: SemEval 2023/2024 Task 3/4 established hierarchical multilabel persuasion detection as the standard. Key findings: hierarchy-aware models outperform flat classifiers; evidence-span extraction is a separate task from classification; multilingual transformers (mBERT, XLM-R) are effective baselines.

techniques.name: SemEval 2024 Task 4 — Multilingual Detection of Persuasion Techniques
techniques.problem: Hierarchical multilabel classification of persuasion techniques in memes
techniques.applicability: HIGH — ManiPsych's taxonomy v2 is already hierarchical (6 families, 26 leaves)
techniques.rationale: SemEval 2024 Task 4 directly validates ManiPsych's hierarchical taxonomy approach. The hierarchy-aware multilabel classification pattern should be the target for the model-backed detection path. Current rule-based detector is a valid baseline but should be honestly labeled as 'Rule-Based Baseline' not 'Model Prediction'.

techniques.name: Evidence-span extraction (token-level annotation)
techniques.problem: Identify the specific text spans that support each detected technique
techniques.evidence_strength: HIGH — SemEval 2023 Task 3 included span-level annotation
techniques.applicability: HIGH — ManiPsych's standalone analyzer already has evidence highlighting; needs to be integrated
techniques.implementation_cost: MEDIUM — joint classification + span extraction model or pipeline
techniques.accessibility_impact: POSITIVE — evidence spans make results explainable
techniques.rationale: Evidence-span extraction is critical for the 'Analyze an Ad' workspace. The standalone analyzer already highlights evidence via regex matching; this should be preserved and honestly labeled as 'Rule-Based Evidence Extraction' until a model-backed span extractor is available.

techniques.name: Multilingual transformer (mBERT/XLM-R) for Spanish ad text
techniques.problem: Detect persuasion techniques in multilingual text including Spanish
techniques.applicability: MEDIUM — ManiPsych corpus is Spanish; mBERT/XLM-R would need fine-tuning on the ManiPsych annotations
techniques.implementation_cost: HIGH — requires GPU fine-tuning, model hosting, inference pipeline
techniques.performance_cost: HIGH — transformer inference not feasible client-side on static GitHub Pages
techniques.privacy_implications: NEGATIVE — if remote inference, user ad text leaves the browser
techniques.rationale: REJECTED for production deployment on static GitHub Pages. A multilingual transformer would require remote inference, violating the privacy constraint (process locally where feasible). Retain as a RESEARCH-ONLY baseline for future server-side deployment. The rule-based detector + evidence highlighting remains the production path.

C_multimodal_detection.summary: CLIP-style image-text fusion is the dominant multimodal approach. Late fusion outperforms early fusion in recent studies. Missing-modality robustness is a critical research area. VLM zero-shot baselines are useful for research but not production.

techniques.name: CLIP-style image-text fusion
techniques.problem: Jointly understand image and text content for ad analysis
techniques.evidence_strength: HIGH — foundational model with extensive follow-up work
techniques.applicability: MEDIUM — ManiPsych corpus is text-heavy; image metadata exists but pixel data is absent
techniques.implementation_cost: VERY HIGH — requires CLIP model, image hosting, inference pipeline
techniques.privacy_implications: NEGATIVE — image upload to remote service
techniques.rationale: REJECTED for production. ManiPsych's corpus has image metadata (image_count, quality_score) but no pixel data. CLIP would require image upload to a remote service, violating the privacy constraint. Retain as RESEARCH-ONLY for future multimodal expansion. The production path honestly marks image analysis as 'Metadata Only — pixel data not available'.

techniques.name: Late fusion (text features + image metadata)
techniques.problem: Combine text features with image metadata for improved classification
techniques.evidence_strength: HIGH — 2025 study shows late fusion outperforms early fusion
techniques.applicability: HIGH — ManiPsych already has image metadata (image_count, quality_score, is_featured) that can be fused with text features
techniques.implementation_cost: LOW — concatenate metadata features with TF-IDF
techniques.privacy_implications: NEUTRAL — metadata only, no pixel data
techniques.rationale: Late fusion of text TF-IDF + image metadata is feasible on static GitHub Pages. The current 'multimodal' cluster space already does this. Should be honestly labeled as 'Text + Metadata Fusion' not 'Multimodal Model'.

techniques.name: Missing-modality robust inference
techniques.problem: Handle cases where image is not provided (text-only ad assessment)
techniques.applicability: HIGH — the 'Analyze an Ad' workspace must handle text-only input gracefully
techniques.implementation_cost: LOW — fallback to text-only path with honest 'Image analysis unavailable' message
techniques.rationale: The 'Analyze an Ad' workspace must honestly handle missing image input. When no image is provided, the system falls back to text-only analysis with a visible 'Image analysis unavailable — text-only mode' indicator. This follows the spec's 'Honest execution modes' requirement.

D_adversarial_improvement.summary: GAN-BERT is a genuine adversarial ML technique for semi-supervised text classification. Constrained LLM generation is a newer, safer alternative. Contrast-set evaluation is the gold standard for robustness testing. The current 'GAN' in ManiPsych is NONE of these — it's phrase injection + regex mutation.

techniques.name: GAN-BERT (genuine adversarial semi-supervised learning)
techniques.problem: Improve text classification with limited labeled data using adversarial training
techniques.evidence_strength: HIGH — peer-reviewed, multiple follow-up papers (PrefGAN-BERT, CDGAN-BERT)
techniques.applicability: LOW — requires GPU training, discriminator model, adversarial loss optimization
techniques.implementation_cost: VERY HIGH — GPU training, model hosting, reproducible checkpoints
techniques.rationale: REJECTED for production. GAN-BERT is a legitimate adversarial ML technique but requires server-side GPU training and hosting. ManiPsych runs on static GitHub Pages. Retain as a RESEARCH-ONLY baseline with a genuine GAN experiment documented in the lab. The current 'GAN' in the standalone analyzer does NOT meet any GAN-BERT criteria and must be renamed.

techniques.name: Constrained LLM adversarial generation
techniques.problem: Generate adversarial text examples using constrained LLM decoding
techniques.applicability: MEDIUM — could generate challenge examples for detector testing
techniques.implementation_cost: HIGH — requires LLM API or local LLM inference
techniques.privacy_implications: NEGATIVE — if remote LLM, ad text leaves browser
techniques.rationale: REJECTED for production due to privacy constraint (no remote inference of user-submitted ad text). Retain as RESEARCH-ONLY for offline challenge-set generation. The production adversarial path remains the 'Rule-Based Adversarial Sandbox' (renamed from 'GAN').

techniques.name: Contrast-set evaluation
techniques.problem: Evaluate model robustness by testing minimal perturbations of inputs
techniques.evidence_strength: HIGH — EMNLP findings, foundational robustness evaluation method
techniques.applicability: HIGH — ManiPsych should build contrast sets for the persuasion detector
techniques.privacy_implications: POSITIVE — uses pre-built challenge sets, no user data
techniques.rationale: Contrast-set evaluation is the honest, feasible approach to detector robustness testing on static GitHub Pages. The Rule-Based Adversarial Sandbox already does a primitive version of this (phrase insertion + re-detection). Should be reframed as 'Contrast-Set Robustness Testing' rather than 'GAN Training'.

techniques.name: Rule-Based Adversarial Sandbox (RENAME of current 'GAN')
techniques.problem: Find detector gaps by inserting phrases and re-running detection
techniques.evidence_strength: LOW — not a published technique, but a useful engineering tool
techniques.applicability: HIGH — already implemented, works client-side
techniques.privacy_implications: POSITIVE — fully local, no remote inference
techniques.rationale: SELECTED for production with CORRECTED NAMING. The existing 'GAN' is not a GAN — it's a rule-based adversarial sandbox that inserts phrases from a predefined list and re-runs regex detection. This is a legitimate detector-gap-discovery tool. Rename to 'Rule-Based Adversarial Sandbox' or 'Adversarial Phrase Perturbation Prototype'. Preserve the behavior, correct the label.

E_synthetic_data_governance.summary: Synthetic data memorization, near-duplication, and distribution shift are critical risks. Quarantine + human review + safety screening are required before any synthetic example reaches training. ManiPsych must not auto-train on user submissions.

techniques.name: Synthetic data memorization screening
techniques.problem: Detect when synthetic data memorizes real training examples
techniques.applicability: HIGH — if ManiPsych ever generates synthetic ads, must screen for memorization
techniques.rationale: If the Rule-Based Adversarial Sandbox generates variants, each must be screened for exact-match and near-duplicate against the real corpus before any use. This is a hard requirement — no synthetic example may be used without memorization screening.

techniques.name: Synthetic-data quarantine + human review pipeline
techniques.problem: Ensure synthetic examples are reviewed, safety-screened, and approved before training
techniques.applicability: HIGH — ManiPsych must document the quarantine workflow even if not actively generating
techniques.implementation_cost: LOW — documented workflow + review queue UI
techniques.rationale: The spec requires a visible quarantine workflow: generated → quarantined → safety-screened → human-reviewed → approved-for-training OR rejected. Even though ManiPsych doesn't auto-train, the workflow must be documented and visible in the 'Models & Adversarial Lab' section.

techniques.name: No automatic training ingestion
techniques.source: Spec Section 12: 'Corrections enter an isolated review queue... never trigger automatic retraining'
techniques.problem: Prevent user submissions from automatically reaching training
techniques.applicability: CRITICAL — hard requirement
techniques.rationale: Hard requirement: user-submitted ad assessments and corrections NEVER reach training automatically. They enter an isolated review queue or downloadable review package. The 'Analyze an Ad' workspace must clearly state 'Your submission is not stored, not sent to analytics, not added to the corpus, and not used for training.'

F_calibration_abstention.summary: Temperature scaling is the standard post-hoc calibration method. ECE and Brier score are standard calibration metrics. Selective classification with risk-coverage curves is the standard abstention approach. Conformal prediction is newer but requires exchangeability assumptions.

techniques.name: Temperature scaling for post-hoc calibration
techniques.problem: Calibrate model confidence scores post-hoc without retraining
techniques.evidence_strength: HIGH — standard technique, cited 99 times in 2024
techniques.applicability: MEDIUM — ManiPsych's current 'confidence' values are rule-based scores, not model probabilities
techniques.rationale: REJECTED for current production because there are no model probabilities to calibrate. The rule-based detector produces heuristic scores (0.0-1.0) that are NOT calibrated probabilities. Temperature scaling would be misleading. When a model-backed detector is available, temperature scaling should be applied. Until then, scores must be labeled 'Rule-Based Score (Uncalibrated)' not 'Confidence' or 'Probability'.

techniques.name: Selective classification / abstention
techniques.problem: Allow the system to abstain when uncertain
techniques.applicability: HIGH — ManiPsych should abstain on short text, ambiguous cases, out-of-distribution input
techniques.rationale: Abstention is critical for honesty. The 'Analyze an Ad' workspace must support an 'Insufficient Evidence' outcome when the text is too short, the techniques are ambiguous, or the input is out-of-distribution. The authorship module already has length-aware abstention (below 15 tokens = INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE). This pattern should extend to the ad grader.

techniques.name: Honest confidence labeling (NO calibration until model exists)
techniques.source: Spec Section 3: 'Never call... a heuristic score calibrated confidence'
techniques.problem: Prevent misleading confidence labels
techniques.applicability: CRITICAL — hard requirement
techniques.rationale: All current scores must be relabeled: 'Rule-Based Score (Uncalibrated)' instead of 'Confidence', 'Heuristic Match' instead of 'Model Prediction', 'Association' instead of 'Causal Effect'. The methodology section already explains this; the UI labels must follow.

G_interactive_tutorials.summary: Driver.js is the lightest, most accessible tutorial library (no dependencies, 5KB). Shepherd.js is more feature-rich but heavier. A custom finite-state engine offers maximum control but requires more development. WCAG 2.2 requires focus management, visible focus, and keyboard support.

techniques.name: Driver.js — lightweight no-dependency tutorial library
techniques.problem: Provide product tours and feature highlights with minimal bundle cost
techniques.applicability: HIGH — 5KB gzipped, no dependencies, works on static sites
techniques.accessibility_impact: MEDIUM — has keyboard support but focus management needs custom work
techniques.rationale: Driver.js is the best fit for ManiPsych's static GitHub Pages constraint. At 5KB gzipped with no dependencies, it adds negligible weight. It supports keyboard navigation, highlights, and popovers. However, the spec requires event-driven advancement, local persistence, and pause/resume/restart — these need a custom state machine wrapping Driver.js. SELECTED as the overlay engine, with a custom FSM for state management.

techniques.name: Shepherd.js — feature-rich tutorial library
techniques.problem: Provide extensive customization and framework integration
techniques.applicability: MEDIUM — more features but heavier (40KB+)
techniques.accessibility_impact: MEDIUM — better built-in accessibility than Driver.js
techniques.rationale: REJECTED in favor of Driver.js due to bundle size (40KB vs 5KB) and the spec's preference for the lightest justified architecture. Shepherd.js's extra features (framework integration, advanced positioning) are not needed for ManiPsych's use case.

techniques.name: Custom finite-state tutorial engine + Driver.js overlay
techniques.problem: Event-driven advancement, local persistence, pause/resume/restart/reset, version migration
techniques.applicability: CRITICAL — hard requirement
techniques.implementation_cost: MEDIUM — custom FSM with localStorage persistence
techniques.rationale: The spec requires event-driven advancement (not just Next-button clicks), local persistence (survive refresh), pause/resume/restart/reset, version migration, and missing-target recovery. Driver.js alone doesn't provide these. A custom FSM (~2KB) wrapping Driver.js for overlay rendering gives full control. State persists in localStorage with version keys. This is the selected architecture for the tutorial system.

techniques.name: WCAG 2.2 focus management for tutorials
techniques.problem: Ensure tutorial is accessible — focus placement, restoration, Escape behavior
techniques.applicability: CRITICAL — hard requirement
techniques.implementation_cost: LOW — focus management in custom FSM
techniques.rationale: WCAG 2.2 requires: visible focus, focus placement on step start, focus restoration on step end, Escape to pause/exit, no content hidden by sticky headers when focused. The custom FSM must implement these. WCAG 2.2 AA is the target.

rejected_techniques_summary.multilingual_transformer: B3 — requires remote inference, violates privacy constraint
rejected_techniques_summary.CLIP_fusion: C1 — requires image upload to remote service, violates privacy
rejected_techniques_summary.GAN_BERT: D1 — requires GPU training, not feasible on static GitHub Pages
rejected_techniques_summary.constrained_LLM: D2 — requires remote LLM, violates privacy
rejected_techniques_summary.temperature_scaling: F1 — no model probabilities to calibrate yet

findings: All selected techniques are feasible on static GitHub Pages without remote inference
The GAN renaming is justified — 0/8 gate criteria met
The rejected techniques (transformer, CLIP, GAN-BERT) are correctly classified as research-only
The tutorial architecture (Driver.js + custom FSM) is the lightest viable option
WCAG 2.2 focus management is included in the tutorial design
Honest labeling (F3) improves accessibility by reducing confusion
Missing-modality handling (C3) provides clear unavailable states
Driver.js has keyboard support; custom FSM adds focus restoration
No accessibility concerns with selected techniques
critique_passes.verdict: PASS — two consecutive critique passes find no unsupported architecture recommendation
